tasks.description:
**Question.** Can colour bars be seen to move only when attention tracks them, while an invisible luminance grating sets the overall motion? (Experiment 1.)

**What is on the screen.** A black-and-white bull's-eye to fixate inside an annulus (4.0-8.4 dva). In the annulus a red-green grating (40 % colour contrast, at the observer's own equiluminance) and a luminance grating, each eight sinusoidal cycles, turn in opposite directions at [[param:rate_hz]]. After 500 ms of bull's-eye and [[param:pre_cue]] of turning gratings, a black pointer pair marks two opposite bars of the target grating and turns with them for [[param:cue_duration]].

**What the subject does.** Keeps fixating the bull's-eye (instructed; no eye tracker) and tracks the marked pair with attention for [[param:track_duration]] after the pointer goes. A test pointer then appears for [[param:test_duration]], on the tracked pair or an adjacent pair of the same polarity; the observer answers yes (J) or no (F).

**Varied.** Luminance contrast, [[param:n_contrasts]] levels from [[param:contrast_min]] to [[param:contrast_max]]; which grating is tracked (this set: colour bars; configs/task-luminance.yaml: luminance bars).

**Measured.** Proportion of test pointers correctly identified at each luminance contrast (the paper's Fig. 1B tracking accuracy).

**What it can and cannot show.** Where colour bars stay trackable while the luminance grating dominates the global rotation, tracking cannot rest on low-level motion alone. Colours are display values matched in luminance, not in cone contrast, so equiluminance holds only as well as the observer's own setting and the rig's photometry.
notes: Paper: 1.0-s pointer, 1.5-s tracking, 240-ms test pointer, 2.0 Hz, 8 cycles, annulus 4.0-8.4 dva, bull's-eye radius 1 dva. ASSUMED: 500-ms bull's-eye period, 500-ms pre-cue, 4-s key deadline, J/F keys, pointer sizes, 4 bull's-eye rings, 500-ms interval.
Target grating (colour or luminance bars) is fixed per session; this file tracks colour bars (configs/task-luminance.yaml tracks luminance bars).
k (equiluminance) comes from the observer's latest equiluminance-speed run; a real session without one is refused.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** At what red-green balance does this observer's colour grating look slowest (the paper's equiluminance criterion)?

**What is on the screen.** The red-green grating alone (40 % colour contrast, eight sinusoidal cycles) turning at 2.0 Hz in the annulus around the bull's-eye.

**What the subject does.** Fixates the bull's-eye and turns a knob (scroll wheel or up/down arrows) on k, the green-to-red luminance modulation ratio, until the grating looks slowest; SPACE commits. Each setting starts at a random k in [[param:k_start_range]] and moves by a factor of [[param:k_step]] per step.

**Varied.** Starting value and rotation direction across settings.

**Measured.** The setting of k; the geometric mean of the settings is the k every other colour task uses.

**What it can and cannot show.** An observer- and display-specific equiluminance point by the paper's criterion. It does not calibrate the display: gun luminances still come from the rig's photometer file.
notes: Paper: minimum apparent speed criterion (p. 1563, note 10). ASSUMED: start range, step, k limits 0.25-4, 60-s limit, 3 settings per direction, 500-ms bull's-eye and interval.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** An alternative equiluminance setting by heterochromatic flicker photometry (not the paper's criterion: a deviation).

**What is on the screen.** The annulus filled uniformly, alternating between the red-heavy and green-heavy states of the 40 % colour modulation at about [[param:flicker_hz]], locked to whole display frames.

**What the subject does.** Fixates the bull's-eye and adjusts k (scroll wheel or up/down arrows) until the flicker is least; SPACE commits.

**Varied.** Starting value of k across settings.

**Measured.** The setting of k (geometric mean).

**What it can and cannot show.** A standard photometric balance; it can differ from the minimum-speed setting the paper used.
notes: Not the paper's method (deviation). 15 Hz, 6 settings, 60-s limit, start range and step are ASSUMED.
The effective rate is refresh/(2 x whole frames per half cycle): 15 Hz at 60 or 120 Hz.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** How much luminance contrast cancels the colour grating's contribution to the overall rotation?

**What is on the screen.** The 40 % colour grating and a luminance grating turning in opposite directions at 2.0 Hz in the annulus.

**What the subject does.** Without tracking individual bars, adjusts the luminance contrast until the global rotation is ambiguous (nulled); SPACE commits.

**Varied.** Start from above ([[param:start_above]]) or below ([[param:start_below]]) and the colour grating's direction; four settings.

**Measured.** The nulling luminance contrast (the paper: 5-10 %, observer-dependent).

**What it can and cannot show.** The point where colour and luminance contribute equally to low-level motion; it sets the scale for the tracking task's contrast range.
notes: Paper: motion null without attending to features (p. 1563). Start values, 3% step, limits, 60-s limit and order are ASSUMED.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** How much contrast does a turning grating need to be noticed (or its direction seen), alone and under a superimposed colour grating? (Fig. 1C.)

**What is on the screen.** One grating turning at 2.0 Hz in the annulus. Cells, in order: the luminance grating alone, the luminance grating with the 40 % colour grating turning the opposite way, and the colour grating alone.

**What the subject does.** Adjusts the grating's contrast until it is just noticed (this file) and commits with SPACE; configs/thresholds-direction.yaml uses the direction criterion.

**Varied.** Cell, and start from above ([[param:start_above]]) or below ([[param:start_below]]).

**Measured.** Threshold contrast per cell, the mean of four settings.

**What it can and cannot show.** How strongly the colour grating masks the luminance grating's visibility. Thresholds near 0.4 % need a 10-bit or bit-stealing display; an 8-bit display cannot reach them.
notes: Paper: four settings per threshold, twice from above and twice from below, luminance alone first. Start values, 5% step, limits and 60-s limit are ASSUMED.
configs/thresholds-direction.yaml runs the direction criterion (luminance cells only); it is a separate parameter set of this task.

Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour. Luminance bars: same chromaticity, ±20% (example start contrast).

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** Does a colour grating's apparent speed drop near equiluminance for global motion but much less when its bars are tracked with attention? (Experiment 2.)

**What is on the screen.** Outer ring: the 40 % colour grating turning at [[param:outer_rate_hz]] with a luminance contrast that varies from trial to trial ([[param:luminance_contrasts]]). Inner ring: a [[param:comparison_contrast]] luminance grating turning the other way.

**What the subject does.** Adjusts the inner ring's rate (scroll wheel or up/down arrows) until it matches the outer ring; SPACE commits. This file: global impression of motion. configs/speed-tracking.yaml: rate of a pair of bars tracked with attention.

**Varied.** Luminance contrast added to the colour grating; match type (global or tracking, by file).

**Measured.** The matched rate of the inner ring at each luminance contrast.

**What it can and cannot show.** A dip in the global match that the tracking match lacks is the paper's dissociation. The 0.5-Hz outer rate is the paper's; the inner ring's size is ASSUMED.
notes: Paper: 0.5 Hz outer rotation, 15% comparison. ASSUMED: inner ring 1.6-3.6 dva, 8 comparison cycles, the nine luminance levels (read off Fig. 2), photometric zero, start range, step, limits, 120-s limit, 3 matches per level.
Inner-ring bar lines are offset only to keep the schematic readable; phases are random per trial.

Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour. Luminance bars: same chromaticity, ±15%.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.
